sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Imports the argument parser, JSON tools, file counter and the package inventory function.
sections.why: Brings in the tools needed to run the inventory and print results.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Run inventory and print summary
sections.what: Reads the source and output paths, runs the inventory, checks that the references are a list, prints the summary without the references, and prints a count of leaf file endings.
sections.why: Likely reason: the summary is short, and the suffix count shows what kinds of files the package holds.
sections.watch_out: The assert check stops the script with a bare error rather than a helpful message.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Command entry point
sections.what: Runs the main function when the file is run directly.
sections.why: Lets the developer start the inventory from the command line.

summary: A command-line tool that inventories a project package and prints a summary plus a count of leaf file types, without reading the documents' instructions.
purpose: Lets a developer see what files a package holds before extraction.
why: Likely reason: the docstring says it never interprets document instructions, so the inventory is a safe, read-only first look.
how: It calls the inventory function with the source package and output path. It prints the result without the reference list, then prints a count of leaf file suffixes.
inputs: A source package path and an output path for the inventory.
outputs: A printed summary and suffix counts. The inventory itself is written by the inventory function.
risks: The assert line stops the script if the references value is not a list, and asserts are skipped when Python runs with optimization.
debug: If output is missing, check the output path and the inventory function's own result. If the count is empty, confirm the package has leaf references.
